title: Velocity probe harness for core models (tokens/sec + p95 monitoring)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Build a lightweight, automated 'velocity probe' harness that measures sustained tokens-per-second and tail latency (p95/p99) for our three core production model families across representative sequence-length mixes. This harness will be the canonical microbenchmark used by CI canaries, daily regression scans, and ad-hoc performance investigations.

Scope: implement workload drivers, standardized prompt sets, measurement plumbing (Prometheus metrics + push gateway), and a regression detector that raises a signal when TPS or p95 deviates beyond defined thresholds. The harness must exercise KV cache warm/cold states, batching variations, and both sampling and deterministic decoding.

Goals:
- Provide repeatable TPS and p95 numbers for model variants (fp16, q4_k, q8_0b) on our standard inference hardware profiles.
- Detect regressions automatically in CI and post results to the bench dashboard.
- Keep runtime cost of each benchmark under a configurable budget (default 30s per model/variant).

Out of scope: full-scale distributed throughput tests (this is a microbenchmark focused on stable tokens/sec and latency profiles).
acceptance_criteria: A harness binary/runner lives in infra/benchmarks/velocity-probe and accepts a YAML workload manifest.
Produces stable time-series: tokens/sec, avg latency, p50/p95/p99, and KV-hit ratio exported to Prometheus with labels (model, quant, hw, seq_profile).
Regression detector evaluates last-N runs and flags >15% TPS drop or >1.3x p95 increase compared to baseline; opens a ticket and posts to #bench-alerts.
CI canary job runs the harness for all core models on every runtime merge and fails the pipeline on regression signals with a triage link.
Runbook added to runbooks/perf/velocity-probe.md describing how to re-run, interpret outliers, and create a performance rollback PR.
test_plan: 1) Create three sequence profiles (short/light, mixed, long-heavy) with representative prompt samples from production logs (anonymized). 2) Implement a replay driver that can throttle to target concurrency and a synthetic driver that emits deterministic prompts for reproducibility. 3) Run baseline sweep on dedicated infra to capture baseline TPS/p95 for each model/quant/hw. 4) Wire metrics into Prometheus + dashboard and add a regression job in CI (nightly + merge canary). 5) Validate detector by injecting controlled latency regressions in a staging runtime and confirm detections and alerts.
implementation_notes:
- Use existing tokenization utilities to ensure token counts match prod telemetry.
- Leverage the runtime's continuous batching hooks; measure TPS both with batching disabled and with configured batch sizes (auto, 32, 64).
- Include KV cache modes: cold-start, warm-reuse, and warmed-by-prefetch.
- Sampling: deterministic top-k/top-p disabled for baseline; add optional sampled workloads to measure variability.
- Keep harness single-file executable for CI, with Docker image published to ghcr.
- Store results as JSON artifacts in CI to allow offline diffing and quick-bisecting.
observability_and_alerting: Metrics: bench_tokens_per_sec, bench_latency_ms{quant,model,hw,seq_profile,kv_mode}, bench_kv_hit_rate. Alerts: bench_regression_tps_drop (>15% vs baseline across 3 consecutive runs) and bench_p95_inflation (>1.3x baseline). Alerts post to #bench-alerts and create a Linear ticket with perf-regression template. Attach diffs and a link to raw artifacts.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: noisy measurements due to infra variability. Mitigation: run N=3 warmup cycles then sample 5 measurement windows, use median-of-means for TPS. Risk: false positives from model flavor changes. Mitigation: label baselines per model-variant and require at least two CI runs to confirm before auto-filing a high-priority ticket.
Risk: probe runtime could be costly if run frequently. Mitigation: default cadence is nightly; per-merge canary runs a reduced-duration variant.
